name: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis
definition: Three-dimensional spinal deformity arising during adolescence without an identifiable secondary cause, defined radiographically by a Cobb angle of at least 10 degrees.

typical: Progression risk relates to growth and curve magnitude

investigations.principle: Standing PA and lateral full-spine radiographs quantify Cobb angle and sagittal balance; MRI is selected for atypical or neurological features.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

green: Bracing for selected skeletally immature progressive curves
amber: Surgery is considered for larger/progressive curves based on magnitude, maturity and balance.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vakra-prishtha phenotype may be documented descriptively; modern curve classification remains primary.

patientEducation.summary: Three-dimensional spinal deformity arising during adolescence without an identifiable secondary cause, defined radiographically by a Cobb angle of at least 10 degrees.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
